title: Add adaptive load-funnel canary and backpressure scheme
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: We see occasional tail-latency and throughput oscillations when incremental traffic is shifted during rollouts at medium QPS (500-2k). Existing canaries detect distribution-level shifts but are noisy under transient bursts. This PR introduces an "adaptive load-funnel" canary detector plus an automated backpressure scheme that gates rollout traffic based on a short-term funnel of throughput and tail-latency signals. Design summary: 1) Load-funnel detector computes a short-window (1m/5m) evaporation funnel of offered load vs accepted throughput, and correlates it with p95/p99 token-latency deltas and error-rate drift. 2) Detection logic uses Bayesian smoothing and a conservative decision rule to declare progressive degradation only when both funnel leak-rate and tail-latency exceed configurable thresholds. 3) Backpressure scheme integrates with the rollout controller: on a canary hit we first throttle canary weight by a ramp-decay policy, then pause further ramps if secondary signals (error spike or throughput collapse) persist for >2 windows. 4) Fallback policy: automatic traffic reroute to fallback variant and open an alert if sustained for >5m. Metrics and thresholds: primary signals: funnel_leak_ratio, p99_delta_ms, accepted_throughput_ratio, 5xx_rate. Default thresholds chosen after offline replay: funnel_leak_ratio > 0.12 AND p99_delta_ms > 45ms triggers soft-throttle; persistent for 2 windows triggers pause+fallback. Rollout plan: roll out as a canary-only feature flag (perf.canary.load_funnel=true) for 10% of internal traffic for 48h, then 50% for 24h, then general. Monitoring dashboards and alert rules added in this change. Tests: unit tests for detector math, integration test that replays synthetic burst traces and asserts correct throttle/pause decisions, end-to-end smoke with a small canary deployment in the perf lab. Backwards compatibility: integrations with existing canary API are additive; defaults disabled for earlier release branches. Implementation notes: detector lives in perf-canary/src/canaries/load_funnel_detector.py, rollout integration in perf-canary/src/controller/backpressure_gate.py, dashboards and alerts under perf-canary/infra/observability/*. This PR contains a moderate-sized refactor to reuse the existing sliding-window store and the metrics exporter. CI and safety: perf-suite was flaky initially (one test timeout) and was re-run; all required checks passed. See review conversation for safety signoff. Related: ENG-1423 (stabilize rollout behavior), ENG-2078 (reduce noisy canary alerts), SUP-558 (customer incident that motivated funnel investigation).

release_notes: Introduce an adaptive load-funnel canary detector and automatic backpressure gating for rollouts. Adds new observability for funnel metrics. Disabled by default; enable via perf.canary.load_funnel=true. Improves robustness of rollouts under transient load spikes.
public_description: Adds an adaptive canary detector that reduces noisy false positives during bursty traffic by correlating load funnel and tail-latency signals, and an automated backpressure gate that gracefully throttles and pauses rollouts when regressions are detected.
notes: Post-merge actions: schedule a 24h internal canary run, monitor load_funnel_dashboards for at least 48h, and be prepared to rollback the feature flag in >=2 clusters if a persistent regression is observed. A follow-up (ENG-2078) will add ML-based threshold auto-tuning.
